drafts.angle: Shared norms before launch (rides @sama 'most important thing OpenAI has published in awhile' + 'shared norms… red-team safety cases… shared transparency standards', 1.52M / 214K / 132K)
drafts.draft_en:
Frontier labs are now talking about shared norms and red-team safety cases before a model ships.

AI ads need the same idea, at a smaller scale:

- checked against brand rules before publish
- checked against legal claims before publish
- checked against platform policy before publish

Approve, fix, or block. Before the ad goes live, not after the takedown.
drafts.video_tip: 30s talking head. Open with the sama quote card on screen for 2s, then cut to you: 'Ads need this too.' Three on-screen checkmarks, one per line, then 'Approve / Fix / Block' as the end card. Native upload, captions burned in, no link in the post.

drafts.angle: One-line builder question (rides @OfficialLoganK 'What are you building with Gemini 4 Neon this weekend?', 469K)
drafts.draft_en: What's the closest an AI-generated ad has come to shipping with something it shouldn't have at your company?
drafts.video_tip: Text-only works best for this pattern. If you add video: 10s selfie clip asking the question straight to camera, question as a caption from frame 1, then reply to the best answers with short follow-ups.

drafts.angle: Agent swarms move the bottleneck to review (rides @levie swarms + orchestration harness, 68K with 1.9x bookmarks-to-likes, and @rauchg's trust/provenance warnings)
drafts.draft_en:
As agents run longer jobs in swarms, the review step is the part that breaks.

An agent can make 500 ad variants before lunch. No team reads 500 ads.

So the check has to scale like the generator: every variant scored against brand rules, legal claims, and platform policy, with a reason attached to every block.

Making creative is solved. Trusting it at volume isn't.
drafts.video_tip: 45s screen recording: a grid of ad variants filling the screen fast, then each tile flips to approve/fix/block with a one-line reason. Voiceover reads the first two lines. End on the last line as text. No music.
